questions.scenario: What are the three types of cost poured into every WIP process bucket?
options: Transferred-in cost, direct costs (labor/materials), applied factory overhead
questions.explanation: Each bucket receives what the previous process handed over, plus the direct labor/materials consumed here, plus overhead APPLIED via a driver like machine hours.
wrongExplanations: Those are bank accounts, not cost categories.
Selling/admin costs never enter product buckets — they're period expenses.
Those are statutory/compliance items (Module 14), not production inputs.

questions.scenario: The dyeing bucket holds: transferred-in fabric ৳40,00,000; dyes ৳6,00,000; labor ৳7,00,000; applied OH ৳7,00,000. Output: 100,000 m fabric, no leftover WIP. Cost per metre leaving?
questions.explanation: (40L + 6L + 7L + 7L) = ৳60,00,000 ÷ 100,000 m = ৳60/m. The bucket passes the WHOLE accumulated total downstream — that's how cost accumulates step by step.
wrongExplanations: That's the transferred-in cost alone divided wrong — you must add THIS process's additions too.
৳40/m ignores dyes, labor and OH added in dyeing.
Check your division: 60L ÷ 100,000 = 600 per… no wait — 60,00,000/100,000 = 60.

questions.scenario: The factory's monthly electricity bill of ৳9 lakh should reach garments by:
options: Direct entry into one lucky order's WIP
Pooling into factory overhead for the period, then applying it into processes via a driver (machine/labor hours)
Ignoring it — electricity isn't a product cost
Splitting equally among all employees' salaries
questions.explanation: Shared factory life becomes overhead, applied proportionally to usage drivers. That's why machine-hour logs feed accounting — they allocate reality fairly across orders.
wrongExplanations: One order absorbing the whole factory's power would wildly distort its cost.
Electricity IS a manufacturing cost — ignoring it understates every garment.
Employees' salaries have nothing to do with allocating power costs.

questions.scenario: Rule R2 fires: 5,000 kg yarn (৳31,00,000) issued from store to knitting for PO-2291. The entry:
questions.explanation: Value moves from raw-material inventory INTO the first process bucket. The order reference on the debit keeps order-level costing possible.
wrongExplanations: The cash left at PURCHASE time (or when payable arose); issuing yarn moves no money.
COGS waits for SHIPMENT (Module 6) — floor issues go through WIP first.
Revenue has nothing to do with internal material movement.

questions.scenario: Cutting consumes 80,000 m out of 100,000 m dyed fabric (৳60/m) for PO-2291. What amount transfers into the cutting/sewing bucket?
questions.explanation: Only consumed quantity carries its accumulated cost forward. The remaining 20,000 m stays in Inventory—Fabric at ৳12,00,000 awaiting other orders.
wrongExplanations: That charges ALL dyed fabric to one order while 20,000 m still sits in store — double-charging someone.
That skips the value dyeing ADDED (dyes, labor, OH) — understated transfer.
Budgets guide decisions; actual accumulated cost is what accounting transfers.

questions.scenario: Month-end: knitting has 10,000 kg of half-processed fabric inside the machines. Where does ITS share of cost sit?
options: Nowhere — unfinished goods carry no cost until finished
As ending WIP in the knitting bucket — its fair partial share stays put; only completed output passes down
questions.explanation: Buckets split their totals between completed output (passes down) and ending WIP (stays). Giving unfinished cloth full-grown costs would overstate both FG and COGS later.
wrongExplanations: The yarn and labor already spent are real — they can't vanish just because work paused.
Optimism is not valuation.
Nothing shipped, so nothing can be expensed as sold.

questions.scenario: Arif quoted $2.85; H&M offers $2.60 (≈৳320). The costing sheet shows true cost ৳400/pc. Correct commercial conclusion:
options: Accept — revenue above yarn cost means profit
Accept — volume will fix it later
Reject or renegotiate: price below fully-loaded cost is a pre-agreed loss per piece
Accept but skip recording the order in WIP
questions.explanation: This is WHY process costing exists: negotiation with open eyes. Every piece sold at ৳320 costing ৳400 burns ৳80 before overheads even finish — multiplied by thousands of pieces.
wrongExplanations: Yarn was only ~৳155/pc of it — ignoring labor/OH is exactly the bucket-blindness this module kills.
'Volume fixes it' works ONLY if marginal economics say so — and full-cost data says the opposite here.
Skipping records doesn't change economics; it just hides the bleeding.

questions.scenario: Applied overhead used machine hours; the year-end bill shows actual OH exceeded applied by ৳14 lakh. This 'under-absorption' most likely indicates:
options: Real signals worth investigating: idle capacity, rate set too low, or unbilled cost increases
questions.explanation: Variances are management radar. Persistent under-absorption means products were charged less overhead than reality delivered — pricing and margin analysis need the cause fixed.
wrongExplanations: 14 lakh is far beyond rounding noise for a composite knit plant.
Maybe — but theft would be ONE specific cause among several ordinary ones; variance flags the question, not the culprit.
Buyers contract prices upfront; absorption correction is an internal matter.

questions.scenario: Mizan's payroll shows ৳12,00,000 sewing-line wages and ৳3,00,000 head-office salaries. How should these flow?
options: Both into the sewing WIP bucket
Sewing wages → cutting/sewing bucket (direct labor); office salaries → admin expense, never touching garment cost
questions.explanation: Direct labor builds product cost; admin salaries support the company generally. Mixing them inflates garment cost AND hides administrative bloat — two lies in one classification error.
wrongExplanations: Office salaries in garment cost would make tees pay for desks.
Sewing wages ARE product cost — expensing them all distorts both inventory value and margins.
Accounting by coin flip explains many historical mysteries, but let's improve.

questions.scenario: Rafiq designs the cost rollup. Which guard makes the system self-defending against impossible flows?
options: Allow any values — accountants check later
Enforce mass conservation: units out ≤ units in + beginning WIP per bucket, and value out = value in + additions (within tolerance), rejecting otherwise
Let each department invent its own formula
questions.explanation: Physical impossibility checks catch misreported production BEFORE it poisons pricing. Money obeys conservation once converted correctly — the engine enforces it like Module 4 enforced sequence.
wrongExplanations: Later-checking found the Gazipur repairs mess years late; prevention beats archaeology.
Randomization is the one thing worse than no system.
One company, one truth: departments may differ in OPERATIONS, never in math.
